title: Has the safety fallback for our automated system actually been tested, not just documented?
description: A board-level oversight question testing whether a documented human-oversight safety requirement for an automated system has been verified in practice, rather than assumed to work because it exists on paper.
question_text: For any automated or driver-assist system we operate or deploy, can management show us evidence that the human-oversight fallback actually catches failures in practice — engagement monitoring data, disengagement logs, near-miss reviews — rather than pointing only to a policy document that says a human is 'in the loop'?
rationale: Both the Uber Tempe fatality and the Tesla Autopilot recall involved a nominally present human-oversight requirement that failed in practice because it wasn't actively monitored or enforced.
follow_up_actions: Request the current automated driving safety case report and confirm it includes tested engagement-monitoring data.
Confirm automatic emergency braking is enabled during all autonomous operation.
Ask how disengagement and near-miss events are logged and reviewed, and by whom.

citations.title: Collision Between Vehicle Controlled by Developmental Automated Driving System and Pedestrian, Tempe, Arizona, March 18, 2018 (NTSB/HAR-19/03)
